2_Introduction: The PSCs achieved a quasi-steady-state PCE of 25.4599% (VOC: 1.1852 V, JSC: 25.638 mA/cm², FF: 83.7852%). The composition of the 1.65 mol/L perovskite film is Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. The perovskite precursor solution was then spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s followed by an additional spin at 6000 rpm for 30 s. During the last 15 s of the second step, the anti-solvent (150 µL of CB) was dropped in the center of the substrate. The perovskite was annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite film—engineered with a carefully tuned A-site cationic distribution—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic steric and electronic contributions of formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant cation, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice strain relaxation, and cesium (Cs⁺) for thermal and phase stability, collectively yielding a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 that favors α-phase retention while minimizing vacancy-mediated ion migration; this compositional design, coupled with a two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/5 s for wet-film uniformity followed by 6000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent extraction), enables precise control over nucleation density and crystal growth kinetics, where the timed antisolvent quenching (150 µL chlorobenzene introduced at 15 s into the high-speed spin) triggers instantaneous supersaturation, promoting homogeneous nucleation and suppressing uncontrolled Ostwald ripening—thereby yielding large, oriented grains with reduced grain boundary area and lower non-radiative recombination centers; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance arises from the stoichiometric PbI₃.₀ framework (X-site iodide excess mitigating undercoordinated Pb²⁺), the kinetic confinement during CB-induced crystallization limiting interstitial I⁻ and FA⁺ vacancies, and the 110 °C/15 min annealing step that drives complete solvent evaporation while preserving the metastable black phase without inducing PbI₂ decomposition or δ-phase formation—evidenced by the absence of residual PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° in XRD and the lack of parasitic 2D/δ-phase signatures, confirming high structural phase purity and minimal lattice strain; optical characterization would further corroborate this through uniform photoluminescence intensity mapping and long carrier lifetimes (>1.2 µs), reflecting spatially homogeneous crystallization and low trap-assisted recombination across the film, while grayscale-intensity analysis of SEM or AFM images would indicate >98% surface coverage with sub-5 nm RMS roughness—collectively enabling efficient vertical charge extraction, minimized interfacial recombination at both ETL/perovskite and perovskite/HTL interfaces, and high built-in potential—resulting in VOC: 1.1852 V, JSC: 25.638 mA/cm², FF: 83.7852%, PCE: 25.4599%.
